full_judgment:
Qazi Shafi Uddin, J-:- This Rule called in question the judgment and order dated 23.11.85 passed by Mr. Ali Ashrof Khan Lodhi, Subordinate Judge, First Court, Barisal in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 142 of 1984 reversing those dated 5.9.1984 of the learned Munsif, Upazila Court Bakergonj in Miscellaneous Case No. 204 of 1984 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 2. The impugned Kabala registered on 17.6.72 gave rise to this present pre-emption case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 6. Mr. A.K. Badrul Huq, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the present petitioners, (opposite party Nos. 68-69), subsequent purchasers of the case land from the preempted Narayan Chandra Pal submits that the court of appeal below has committed illegality occasioning failure of justice in putting reliance on the testimonies of P.Ws. 1, 2 and 3 dis-carding the evidence of opposite party Nos. 1, 2 and 3 on point of knowledge relating to the transfer of the case land. Mr. Badrul Huq, the learned Advocate also submits that the court of appeal below commit-ted error of law in accepting the plea of knowledge about the impugned kabala dated 17.2.72 given by the petitioners. It is argued that the petitioners having failed to state positively the actual date of his knowledge, the court should not have allowed the pre-emption. Mr. Badrul Huq argues that unless a definite and specific date is expressed, the knowledge of the petitioners can not be computed and the learned Judge fell in error in believing the testimonies of the pre-emptor-petitioners while allowing the appeal. Mr. Badrul Huq also argues that the learned Judge (court of appeal) has committed a serious error of law in appreciating the evidence on record to the great prejudice of the opposite parties. 

 8. One of the statutory requirements for filing a pre-emption case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is that the petitioner has to file the same within 4 months from the date of registration of the kabala or from the date of his knowledge about the transfer of the land in question. In the instant case, the pre-emptor admittedly has not filed the case within 4 months from the date of transfer of the case land but he is alleged to have filed the same within 4 months from the date of his knowledge of the said transfer. The pre-emptor-petitioner has stated in his evidence that he came to know about the said transfer of the case land in the last part of Magh, 1382 B.S. and he is being corroborated by his witnesses at least by P.W.3. The learned Judge believed the testimonies of the pre-emptor-petitioner and his witnesses. The Court below is vested with jurisdiction to appreciate the evidence on record and if he has arrived at a conclusion by accepting the statements of any particular party discarding the testimonies of other party, I do not find any illegality to have been committed by the said learned Judge. In matters of appreciation of evidence this court can hardly interfere with such findings of facts. 

 10. The initial knowledge that the pre-emptor had while he heard about the said transfer in the last part of Magh, 1382 B.S. attained maturity on 26.2.76 when he obtained the certified copy of the kabala transferring the land in question. In order to collect the full particulars for filing a pre-emption case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the petitioner has to know the names of the vendees, the number of plot of land and the quantum of land sold by the vendor in order to examine as to whether he is a contiguous owner of the property sold or not. Unless he is definite as to whether he qualifies himself to file a petition under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, he can not file a proper petition. His initial knowledge that the plot in question was sold would not help him at all in a bid to file a pre-emption case. "Knowledge" as referred to in sub-section 1 of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act means and includes a definite and complete knowledge in order to qualify the petitioner to file an application under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Since the petitioner has given a specific date by stating that on 26.2.76 he obtained the certified copy of the kabala and he obtained the precise and complete knowledge as referred to in sub-section 1 of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as being obtained on that date by the petitioners. And the learned Subordinate Judge has rightly computed four (4) months from the date of precise and complete knowledge so obtained on 26.2.76 for the purpose of limitation. I do not find any reason to disagree with him in the context of the decision cited in 29 DLR as aforesaid. Therefore, the petition under section 96 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is perfectly maintainable. 

 11. Since the court of appeal below being the last court of fact and the decision he has arrived at on the question of facts is not liable to be interfered with by this court, Mr. Badrul Huy the learned Advocate lastly argues that the opposite party Nos. 68-69 who purchased the case land from Narayan Chandra Pal, opposite party No. 1 during the pendency of the case, may be permitted to withdraw the money deposited by the pre-emptor-petitioners while he filed the pre-emption case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 12. In this Revisional application (paragraph 14), the opposite party Nos. 68-69 (present petitioners) have stated "the service of notice of the Misc. Case upon the vendee opposite party had been caused on 8.8.76 and the kabala in favour of this petitioners is dated 26.7.76 and the kabala in favour of the petitioners was prior to the service of notice." Mr. A.K. Badrul Huq, the learned Advocate argues that the present petitioners had absolutely no knowledge about the pendency of the pre-emption case. lie relies on a decision in the case of Hajera Bibi Petitioner Vs. Noor Jahan Begum & others, Respondents, 35 DLR (HC) 238, wherein his Lordship held, "If at any time after an application for pre-emption has been made, the property is again transferred, such subsequent transferee may be made a party to the pending pre-emption proceeding and the money al- ready deposited may be paid to such subsequent transferee, who is not entitled in such proceeding to any money in excess of the original deposit."
